question.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡4x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{4x}\cdot 4=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e/4$ | ${e}^{3}/4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $3$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}\frac{3}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)}\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{e/4}^{{e}^{3}/4}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =3{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =3(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =3(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡1) \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
